title: Ines and the Garden
premise: Dominic Underhill, a debt-bound scribe for the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers the guild has been quietly selling souls to the court beneath the mountain to keep its ledgers balanced — and that the soul of Ines, a gardener who once saved their life, is the latest entry. When the border wards fall and the stars go out, the collapse tears open the road down, and Dominic descends with a stolen ledger page as their only weapon. Bargaining with a court that trades in memory and time, Dominic learns the price of every survival they've bought was paid by someone else. They win Ines back by surrendering the debt that binds them, choosing justice outside any law, and the two return to a starless world where they must plant something new.
about_author: Odile Okonkwo is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing debts in municipal records before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about paperwork, gardens, and the people history forgets to count.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A night of routine bookkeeping in the guildhall reveals an entry written in no hand Dominic knows: one soul, sold, payment deferred. The emotional beat is quiet dread — the first crack in the world Dominic thought was merely tedious.

chapters.title: Ines at the Wall
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: Ines, the temple gardener who fed Dominic during their hungriest year, now missing from the city rolls. Dominic's POV; grief sharpening into suspicion that the guild took her.

chapters.title: Wards Fall, Stars Go Out
chapters.summary: The border wards shatter and every star vanishes in the same breath. Dominic's POV amid panic in the guildhall as masters burn papers and open doors that should stay shut. Beat: terror and the vertigo of realizing the guild caused it.

chapters.title: What the Guild Trades
chapters.summary: Dominic steals the master ledger and finds decades of soul-sales propping up the guild's impossible inventory. POV shifts briefly to the Guildmaster, coldly pragmatic. Beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: A Page Torn Out
chapters.summary: Dominic cuts Ines's contract page from the ledger — the only proof of claim — and flees as wardens hunt them through burning archives. Beat: desperate flight, first act of open rebellion.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath
chapters.summary: The fallen wards have opened a stair under the old temple garden. Dominic's POV descending past roots that remember being tended. Beat: reluctant courage; the garden itself seems to want Ines back.

chapters.title: Toll of Names
chapters.summary: At the threshold, a gatekeeper demands a true name as toll. Dominic gives a false one and pays in a memory instead — losing their mother's face. Beat: the price of survival made literal and personal.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Arrival in a court lit by bottled stars — the stolen ones. Dominic's POV navigating etiquette where every courtesy is a trap. Beat: awe laced with horror at what beauty costs here.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Debt
chapters.summary: Dominic finds Ines working the court's underground orchard, alive but half-forgotten, her name worn thin. Her POV, disoriented, recognizing Dominic only slowly. Beat: reunion shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Terms of Trade
chapters.summary: Dominic presents the torn page and petitions for Ines's release. The court offers a counter-deal: Ines walks free if another soul fills her place. Beat: moral crisis — survival offered at someone else's expense.

chapters.title: The Other Bidders
chapters.summary: Rival petitioners arrive: a guild warden sent to erase evidence, and a noble buying back his own sold son. Multiple POVs collide. Beat: Dominic realizes they are not alone in this economy of souls.

chapters.title: Ines Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines's POV recovering memories in the orchard — she sold herself willingly to pay the guild's debt for Dominic's life years ago. Beat: devastating reversal; the rescue was always mutual.

chapters.title: Midnight Audit
chapters.summary: Dominic uses scribe skills to audit the court's own books and finds the Undercourt King himself is in default — his crown mortgaged to something older below. Beat: hope; even kings owe.

chapters.title: The Warden's Knife
chapters.summary: The guild warden attacks to destroy the contract page. Ines defends Dominic with a gardener's tools; the warden falls into the deep dark below. Beat: violence, guilt, and the point of no return.

chapters.title: Bargaining with the Deep
chapters.summary: Something older than the court surfaces to collect the King's default. Dominic proposes an audacious trade: the guild's entire ledger of debts, surrendered whole. Beat: gambler's clarity — end the system or die in it.

chapters.title: The King's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: The cornered King offers Dominic anything — wealth, freedom from debt, Ines restored — if they withdraw the audit. Beat: temptation at its most seductive; justice versus comfort.

chapters.title: What Dominic Owes
chapters.summary: Dominic confronts their own original debt and realizes accepting mercy would restart the cycle. They formally enter themselves into the court's books alongside Ines. Beat: self-sacrifice chosen freely, not coerced.

chapters.title: The Reading of Accounts
chapters.summary: Climax begins: a public reckoning before the court where all debts are read aloud, including the guild's crimes and the King's default. Dominic's voice steadies. Beat: justice outside the law, spoken plainly.

chapters.title: Stars Returned
chapters.summary: The deep thing accepts the ledger and dissolves the court's power; bottled stars burst free and streak upward toward the sky. Beat: cathartic release as light returns to the world above.

chapters.title: The Price Paid
chapters.summary: Aftermath below: the King is unmade, the guild's masters above wake to find their trades voided. Dominic and Ines climb the stair, carrying nothing but each other and empty hands. Beat: exhaustion, tenderness, freedom.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Resolution: in a starlit but changed city, the two rebuild the temple garden, taking in others the old systems discarded. Ines's POV mostly. Beat: belonging built rather than granted.

chapters.title: The Garden Keeps Its Own Books
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating voices: a new ledger opens — not of debts but of seeds saved, names remembered, favors given freely. Beat: quiet triumph; survival redefined as what we grow together.
